title: Tate resolution with a prescribed finite polynomial augmentation
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $S$ be a commutative $R$-algebra, and let $\pi:P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow S$ be an $R$-algebra surjection, with $n\geq0$. There exists a divided-power differential graded $R$-algebra $A$ [def-sfb-divided-power-dga] and an augmentation $\varepsilon:A\to S$ (where $S$ is concentrated in degree zero), with $A_0=P$ and $\varepsilon_0=\pi$, such that $H_0(A)\xrightarrow{\sim}S$ via $\varepsilon$ and $H_i(A)=0$ for every $i>0$. The underlying graded divided-power algebra is polynomial, obtained from $P$ by adjoining finitely many variables in each positive degree, and every $A_i$ is free as an $R$-module. In particular, $\cdots\to A_2\to A_1\to A_0\xrightarrow{\pi}S\to0$ is an augmented free $R$-module resolution.

source.place: Tag 09PN (lemma-tate-resolution), statement (1)-(4), finiteness assertion, and its explicit free monomial construction

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], $P$ is Noetherian: it has the required presentation with zero defining ideal. Hence $K=\ker(\pi)$ has a finite ideal generating list $f_1,\ldots,f_r$, by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]; the list may be empty. Put $A(0)=P$ in degree zero with zero differential and zero positive divided powers. This satisfies [def-sfb-divided-power-dga] since its positive-degree part is zero.

source.place: Tag 09PN (lemma-tate-resolution), start of construction and choice of kernel generators

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-adjoin-dga-cycle] successively to adjoin degree-one exterior variables $u_1,\ldots,u_r$ with $d(u_j)=f_j$. Each $f_j$ remains a cycle in degree zero. Call the result $A(1)$. The map which is $\pi$ on $P$ and zero in positive degrees is an augmentation: the only differential whose image can have nonzero augmentation is $d:A(1)_1\to P$, and its image is precisely $(f_1,\ldots,f_r)=K$. Thus $H_0(A(1))=P/K\cong S$ via the given $\pi$. The direct-sum descriptions in [lem-sfb-divided-power-variable-adjunction] show that each term has as a $P$-basis the exterior monomials in the $u_j$ of that degree, and so is finite free.

source.place: Tag 09PN (lemma-tate-resolution), construction of A(1) and base case

proof.text: Inductively suppose $m\geq1$ and $A(m)$ is a divided-power DGA augmented to $S$, obtained from $P$ by adjoining finitely many variables in each degree $1,\ldots,m$, with $H_0(A(m))\cong S$ via the augmentation and $H_i(A(m))=0$ for $0<i<m$. Its degree-$q$ term is finite free over $P$, by iterating the direct-sum descriptions of [lem-sfb-divided-power-variable-adjunction]: its basis is the products of exterior variables (exponents zero or one) and divided-power symbols, of total degree $q$; there are finitely many variables and every positive-weight exponent is bounded by $q$. In particular $A(m)_m$ is a finite $P$-module. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite], its cycle submodule $Z_m=\ker(d:A(m)_m\to A(m)_{m-1})$ has finite generators $z_1,\ldots,z_t$. Their images generate $H_m(A(m))$ over $P$, since taking a quotient sends a generating list to a generating list.

source.place: Tag 09PN (lemma-tate-resolution), induction hypothesis and finite cycle representatives

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-adjoin-dga-cycle] $t$ times with $e=m+1$ and cycles $z_j$ to form $A(m+1)$ with $d(v_j)=z_j$. Extend the augmentation by zero on all positive degrees. It is a chain map since the new differentials have positive degree. By the module formulas of [lem-sfb-divided-power-variable-adjunction], terms and differentials below degree $m+1$ are unchanged. In degree $m+1$ the new summands are exactly $Pv_j$, so the boundaries in degree $m$ become $d(A(m)_{m+1})+\sum_jPz_j=Z_m$. Consequently $H_m(A(m+1))=0$, and $H_i(A(m+1))=H_i(A(m))$ for $i<m$. The new finite list of variables has degree $m+1$, completing the induction.

source.place: Tag 09PN (lemma-tate-resolution), induction step and low-degree homology calculation

proof.text: Take $A$ to be the union of these monomial inclusions $A(0)\subseteq A(1)\subseteq\cdots$, with its graded divided powers supplied by [lem-sfb-divided-power-variable-adjunction](4). Multiplication, differential and divided powers are defined in any stage containing the input elements; the inclusions preserve them by [lem-sfb-adjoin-dga-cycle], so the results are independent of the stage. Every identity of [def-sfb-divided-power-dga] involves finitely many inputs and holds in a stage containing them, hence holds in $A$. Since $A$ is obtained from $P$ by successive adjunctions of finite sets of variables of one positive degree each, followed by the union, its underlying graded divided-power algebra is polynomial in the sense of [def-sfb-divided-power-dga]. The compatible augmentations likewise give $\varepsilon:A\to S$, with $A_0=P$ and $\varepsilon_0=\pi$. For fixed $i\geq0$, the three terms in degrees $i-1,i,i+1$ and their differentials are already final at stage $A(i+1)$, since later variables have degree at least $i+2$. Thus $H_i(A)=H_i(A(i+1))$, which is $S$ for $i=0$ and zero for $i>0$ by the induction.

source.place: Tag 09PN (lemma-tate-resolution), final colimit paragraph, written as the degreewise stationary union

proof.text: Only finitely many variables were added in each positive degree. In degree $i$, their monomials of total degree $i$ form a finite $P$-basis: only variables of degree at most $i$ occur, exterior exponents are at most one, and divided-power exponents are at most $i$. This follows directly by iterating the direct-sum descriptions in [lem-sfb-divided-power-variable-adjunction]. By [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], ordinary monomials in $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ form an $R$-basis of $P$. Multiplying these ordinary monomials by the indicated positive-degree basis monomials gives an $R$-basis of $A_i$: expanding a finite $P$-linear sum into coefficients proves spanning, and independence follows first over $P$ and then over $R$. Hence all $A_i$ are $R$-free. Surjectivity of $\pi$, $\ker(\pi)=d(A_1)$ and $H_i(A)=0$ for $i>0$ give exactness of the asserted augmented free resolution.

lean.note: Uses the recorded DividedPowerDGA and variable-adjunction presentations. The injective polynomial map identifies its image with exactly A_0, and its composite with the augmentation is the prescribed pi. The H_0 linear equivalence is characterized on actual cycle classes by the augmentation. The normalized union tower starts at the prescribed polynomial algebra and adjoins a finite set in degree k+1 at step k. Module.Free and exactness at the augmentation record the free resolution consequence; positive exactness is the stated vanishing of the recorded homology.
